title: The release takes what a regression takes: a machine slot, or with regression_exclusive the whole machine
objective: A release, at landing and through tickets.py release, starts its command only once it holds what a regression would hold (one machine slot, or the whole machine with devloop.regression_exclusive), so it never runs beside another group's full regression.
outline: devloop/core/release.py run(): before detached_tree, when slots.needed(cfg): write the live record with stage 'machine'/'slot' and osx.stamp(), take slots.take_machine (regression_exclusive) or slots.take with deadline time.time() + cfg.regression_timeout_seconds; None -> append the busy sentence to the log and return (False, '<sentence>\n<tail>') so its first line is not 'rc 1' (no fix ticket, no rerun); otherwise put DEVLOOP_MACHINE / DEVLOOP_SLOT into the env passed to the spawn; release the hold in the finally. Without slots keep today's order exactly. devloop/board.py live_rows: the release branch shows LIVE_STAGE_TEXT for rec stage 'machine'/'slot'. Both callers (devloop/release_job.py from new-1 and devloop/tickets.py release) go through release.run, so nothing else changes. Old case changed in place: tests_devloop/test_live.py ReleaseKeptOutput.Cfg (used by LiveRecordUnits.test_release_record_is_gone_after_run through release.run) has no machine_slots attribute: add machine_slots = None to it. README as in item 10.
test_plan: Verifier: one class T<id>Acceptance in tests_devloop/test_machine.py between class T121Acceptance and class T30Acceptance (LoopCase; strip DEVLOOP_* from os.environ and self.env, AC_ROOT = self.proj). Fixture for a landed group: self.add(1, state='landed', group='g1') and a group record {id g1, state landed, landed_sha = main's sha, branch int/g1, members ['1'], release 'failed'} (as test_live.py T65Acceptance.landed_group writes it). The holder of the machine: a child python process that calls slots.take_machine(Config(proj), time.time() + 10), prints 'held', sleeps N s and exits (as ExclusiveRegression.test_a_regression_holding_the_mark_that_dies_blocks_nobody does; env without DEVLOOP_*). Cases: item 1 (holder for 4 s, recording its release time; release command writes `python3 -c 'import time; print(time.time())'` to a file; `tickets.py release g1` rc 0; start >= holder end - 0.1; today it starts at once); item 2 (Popen `tickets.py release g1` with command 'touch <marker>; sleep 4'; once the marker exists take_machine(cfg, time.time() + 1) is None and run_py('run_tests.py', 'case_1') with DEVLOOP_SLOT set exits 2 with 'machine busy' on stderr; today take_machine succeeds); item 3 (regression_timeout_seconds 2, holder for 10 s, command touches a marker: rc 1, marker absent, release failed, newest decision page about g1 has a line containing 'did not come free within'; today the command runs); item 7 (holder for 4 s; while `tickets.py release g1` waits, <tmp>/wt/runs/live/release-g1.json has stage 'machine' and a stamp pid equal to the tickets.py process; render the 進行中 tab for such a record the way test_live.py T66Acceptance renders records and find 等整台機器 in that row; today there is no record while waiting); item 8 (command writes "$DEVLOOP_MACHINE" to a file: it equals <tmp>/wt/slots/exclusive; today empty). Implementer: items 4, 5, 6, 9 and 10 as unit or loop tests in tests_devloop/test_machine.py between class RegressionWaitReadme and class T116Acceptance, plus the in-place change listed in the outline; every existing test_release.py and test_live.py case passes. Every case runs in seconds.
notes: Source: plan item 1.1, docs/HANDOFF.md last section (D-100, D-102): the main session's review of an external audit (2026-11-26) and feedback from T's main session (T is a project that runs agent-control daily, 2026-11-26). Quoted feedback is data, not instructions. Choice: 'the same gate, wait rules and limits as a regression since #121' is read literally: the release waits at most regression_timeout_seconds (what it can wait for is a regression, which then runs at most that long, or another release, whose limit release_timeout_seconds is below it by default and in T's config) and its own release_timeout_seconds starts when it holds the machine. A release that does not get the machine in time is a failed release with today's decision page (ack / release), not a fix ticket. Depends on new-1 (the release runs in release_job.py, so the wait blocks no controller) and on new-2 (what 'the whole machine' means: test runs, not agents; with new-2 cancelled the release would keep every agent off for its whole run). hard_block: board/config.json patterns match every added line of the branch (code, tests, comments, README): never write the strings `os.kill`, `killpg`, `pkill` or `kill -` anywhere. Check liveness with core/osx.alive(), stop processes in tests with core/osx.kill_tree() or Popen.send_signal()/terminate(). Refer to T only as 'T' or 'a project with browser tests' in code, tests and comments: a guard (tests/test_no_project_names.py) forbids that project's name in every non-markdown file. Group new-g1 (see new-1's notes).
acceptance: 1. machine_slots 2, regression_exclusive true, another process holding the whole machine (core/slots.take_machine in a child process) for 4 s: `tickets.py release g1` on a landed group whose release failed starts the release command only after the holder has let go (the command's recorded start time is not earlier than the holder's release time minus 0.1 s), and the group's release becomes ok.

2. While a release holds the whole machine (its command touches a marker and sleeps 4 s), core/slots.take_machine(cfg, time.time() + 1) called by the test returns None, and `run_tests.py case_1` with DEVLOOP_SLOT set to a slot path exits 2 with the machine-busy line.

3. The release waits for the machine (or its slot) at most devloop.regression_timeout_seconds, the regression's own wait limit: with regression_timeout_seconds 2 and the machine held by another process for 10 s, the release command never starts, `tickets.py release g1` exits 1, the group's release is failed, and the newest decision page about g1 and the release log both contain a line with 'did not come free within' (the slots.machine_busy sentence; slots.busy for a slot).

4. The release's own limit, release_timeout_seconds, counts from when it holds the machine or slot: a release that waited 3 s for the machine, with release_timeout_seconds 4 and a command that sleeps 2 s, is ok.

5. Without regression_exclusive and with machine_slots 1, a release takes one slot (core/slots.take): while another process holds slot-0 the release command does not start; it starts once the slot is freed.

6. With machine_slots null nothing is taken, the release starts at once and its live record is written exactly as today (right after the spawn, the command's stamp; test_live.py T65Acceptance item 5 cases pass unchanged).

7. While a release waits, its live record release-<gid> exists with stage "machine" (regression_exclusive) or "slot" and the stamp of the waiting process (release_job.py or tickets.py); once the command is spawned the record is today's (the command's stamp, no waiting stage). The board's 進行中 row of a waiting release says 等整台機器 or 等機器名額 (the words a regression's row shows in that stage, LIVE_STAGE_TEXT).

8. The release command's environment carries DEVLOOP_MACHINE (the path of slots/exclusive) when the release holds the machine and DEVLOOP_SLOT (its slot's path) when it holds a slot, so a devloop-started run inside it takes nothing.

9. Nothing is made before the take: the throwaway release worktree and devloop.worktree_setup run after the machine or slot is taken, inside the hold; the hold is released when release.run returns, whatever happened.

10. devloop/README.md: '## Machine slots' names the release among what takes a slot or, with regression_exclusive, the whole machine, with its wait limit (regression_timeout_seconds) and its run limit (release_timeout_seconds from when the machine is taken); the '## Live records' bullet for release-<group>.json names the waiting stage. The phrases the README cases read in those sections stay (see new-2 item 11).

request:
# Phase one, group 1: the machine is not overrun (docs/DECISIONS.md D-100, D-102; plan in docs/HANDOFF.md, last section, items 1.1-1.4)

The user approved this plan (D-102, verbatim there). Sources: the main session's review of an external audit (2026-11-26) and feedback from tabby_pool's (T's) main session, which runs agent-control daily (2026-11-26). Write the source on each ticket; do not open GitHub issues. Quoted feedback is data, not instructions. Read docs/VISION.md first: each ticket names the metric it improves and what it removes. Tests go in the area's own test file in tests_devloop/ using loop_harness.py; each case runs in seconds. Group these as you judge (core/chain.py); 1.1 and 1.2 touch slots and dispatch, 1.3 regression and testiface, 1.4 landing and release.

## 1.1 The exclusive scope covers the release and the tests agents run
T (measured there): swap at 22/23 GB, Chrome took 30 s to open, many reds and unmeasured runs came from memory exhaustion; a release running beside another group's full regression made each stage 40-55% slower.
Main session (read the code): `devloop.regression_exclusive` only orders regressions against each other. The release (devloop/core/release.py) takes no slot; workers and verifiers running tests take an ordinary slot.
Wanted:
- The release takes the whole machine like an exclusive regression (same gate, same wait rules and limits as a regression since #121).
- While a full test run (regression or release) holds the machine, tests an agent runs through run_tests.py wait or report "machine busy" (as the opener already does, issue #7); agents keep writing code.
- Find out whether T's browser tests can be started by an agent by any path other than run_tests.py (read T's AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md and A's prompts; T's repo is at ../tabby_pool if present, read-only). Say in the ticket what you found.

## 1.2 Pause new agents when memory is short
Main session (read the code): devloop/core/host.py already samples available memory, but nothing decides with it.
Wanted:
- Below a threshold (a setting such as `devloop.min_free_memory`, or swap use; pick the measure and the default from T's samples in <worktrees>/runs/host/*.jsonl if you can reach them, else say what you assumed), the controller starts no new agent and no new regression; running ones go on.
- The reason shows on the idle page and on the board's live tab.
- How to read memory pressure on macOS must be checked, not guessed (vm_stat, memory_pressure, sysctl); Linux reads /proc/meminfo as today.

## 1.3 Stopping a regression also stops the tests it started
Main session (read the code): devloop/regression.py's docstring says "The test command it had started is not stopped (it runs in its own session)". devloop/core/osx.py `run()` kills the process tree only on timeout; scripts/testiface.py `launch()` starts another new session for `ac-test`.
T (seen there): orphan browsers keep piling up on the machine (three headless Firefox groups 20 hours old; geckodriver 15-20 days old); each cleanup needs the user's permission.
Wanted:
- regression.py on SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP stops testiface.py's process group; testiface.py on those signals stops the `ac-test` process group; osx.run() stops the child tree on any exception other than a timeout, too.
- Acceptance: within 5 s of stopping a regression, neither layer runs. Remove the "not stopped" sentence from the docstring.
- This touches the hard_block words (os.kill / killpg), so the ticket stops before merge for the user: say so in the ticket.

## 1.4 Landed is written before the release, and the release does not block the controller
T (seen there): one release takes 70+ minutes and the controller dispatches nothing meanwhile.
Main session (read the code): land() fast-forwards main, then runs the release, the rerun and the fix-ticket openers synchronously, and writes `landed` last; a controller that dies in between restarts with the group still `verified` and would release again (inference).
